review.headline: The Commissioner Finally Did It (And We Have Questions)
review.deck: Fourteen teams, a $200 auction, one thousand FAAB dollars each, an injury apocalypse, and a final standings page that reads like a police report. This is the official record of the 2025 season. Nobody comes out clean.

podium.note: The commissioner wins the league the same year he runs it. Noted. His auction board was the most boring document ever produced — biggest buy $36 Ladd McConkey, not one player over $40 — and it worked, which is the most insulting part. He coupon-clipped his way to a title with James Cook at $31 and Jalen Hurts at $22 while everyone else lit $60 bills on fire. Renamed the team from Hail Mary to Hail Purdy mid-glow-up. The audit is ongoing.

Paid $56 for Jahmyr Gibbs, $49 for Puka Nacua, burned his FAAB to an even $0, dragged himself into the final — and lost it. Then he built this entire website, which means he commissioned a permanent public monument to his own second-place finish. Respect. Also: therapy.

The best team of 2025 and it is not close: most points in the league, tied-best record, Amon-Ra at $51 and a $44 Jonathan Taylor that printed points all season. Finished third. That is not bad luck, that is a war crime committed by the bracket. He also finished the year with $940 of his $1,000 FAAB untouched — the man guarded that budget like it was enamel.

toilet.note: Four wins. FOUR. With $66 Bijan Robinson — the best running back purchase available to humanity — on the roster. That is like being handed the keys to a Ferrari and reversing it into a lake. The 2025 Toilet Bowl is his, engraved, no appeals.

story: Start with the money, because this league is incapable of spending it responsibly. Fourteen $200 auction budgets went to war on draft night and the receipts tell you everything: 'A dad' dropped a league-record $70 on Ja'Marr Chase, Leo the Cleo went $66 on Bijan, Bullish put $62 on Saquon Barkley. Of the three biggest buys in league history, exactly zero of their owners saw the semifinals. Meanwhile the commissioner quietly assembled a team of $30 misfits and won the whole thing. The market was inefficient and Andrew was the only one who read the prospectus.

Then October arrived and started collecting knees. Tyreek Hill's ACL detonated in Week 4 and took Bullish's $30 with it. Malik Nabers' knee went shortly after — there went $49 of Bend The Knee's budget, a team name that aged into prophecy. Joe Burrow's toe ended Kim Jong Nate's $18 lottery ticket and simultaneously kneecapped the value of that $70 Chase. Half this league's draft capital was in a hospital by Halloween. The Injured Reserved — a team literally named for this exact scenario — went 21-7. You cannot write this.

The regular season belonged to Neil. 1,941.94 points, most in the league, scored with the calm of a man who bills by the fifteen-minute increment. But fantasy playoffs are a casino, and the casino chose violence: the league's best team got clipped before the final, won the bronze game out of spite, and left the arena. The final itself was Andrew's value board against Abhishek's stars-and-scraps roster, and the boring spreadsheet beat the highlight reel. The champion's biggest player cost less than Leo the Cleo's THIRD most expensive player. Sit with that.

At the bottom, the standings page files three separate incident reports. Poop Squad paid $50 for Brian Thomas Jr.'s sophomore season and got a long-term hold. Miley's 5K Speedo Fan Club posted the lowest points-for in the league (1,476.6) despite a $59 CeeDee Lamb, proving you can overpay for a logo. And Leo the Cleo went 4-24 in a way that should trigger a wellness check. The Toilet Bowl was not contested. It was donated.

draft.intro: The 2025 auction, graded with the benefit of hindsight and zero mercy. $200 budgets, 16 roster spots, and some decisions that should have required a co-signer.

rows.verdict: No buy over $36 and a ring. Extreme couponing as a championship strategy.
Two anchors, real value underneath. Docked half a grade for how the story ends.
Best board in the league. The $44 Jonathan Taylor alone should hang in a museum. Didn't even need his whole wallet.
Paid full sticker for Jefferson and got exactly what the sticker said.
No star cost more than $40 and the team went 21-7. All floor, no ceiling, no shame.
$70 is a car payment. Then Cincinnati's quarterback situation happened to it.
Elite QB, big-money rookie, .500 record. Left $6 unspent, which is somehow the most on-brand detail.
Lamar at $32 was theft. The rest of the board was community service.
The Burrow ticket was voided by a toe. $55 CMC in 2025 was a faith-based initiative.
$59 CeeDee and the league's LOWEST points-for. That takes coordination.
$49 on Nabers' knee ligaments. The team name was a warning label.
$92 of it was gone by Halloween — Tyreek's knee and Saquon's regression. A margin call in jersey form.
Paid WR1 money for Brian Thomas Jr.'s gap year. The team name self-reported.
Rostered the best RB season money could buy and won four games. Under league review for Bijan neglect.

farewells.headline: The Departed: A Roasting Toast
farewells.intro: Two chairs empty out this season. League bylaws require they be roasted on the way through the door. Raise a glass.

people.name: Neil
people.title: The Dentist
people.toast: Neil leaves the way he played: efficient, painless, and criminally under-celebrated. The man scored more points than anyone in 2025, went 22-6, and got sent to the bronze podium anyway — the first recorded case of a dentist getting drilled. He exits with $940 of FAAB unspent, because of course the dentist left with the healthiest budget in league history: never touched, twice-a-year checkups only. Somewhere there's a waiver wire he told to 'rinse.' The league loses its best flosser and its cleanest operator in one chair. Prognosis on his replacement: cavities everywhere. To Neil — may your new league appreciate 1,941 points more than we did, and may you finally extract the one thing you couldn't here: a ring.

people.name: Mohsin
people.title: The Bear In Bull's Clothing
people.toast: Mohsin named his team Bullish and then delivered the single most bearish season in franchise history: 8-20, a $62 Saquon that regressed, a $30 Tyreek whose knee filed for bankruptcy in Week 4, and a portfolio that got margin-called before the bye weeks. The man was long optimism and short results for years — every August he'd announce the market bottom was in, and every December he WAS the market bottom. He leaves as the league's greatest contrarian indicator: whatever Mohsin was buying, you sold, and you made the playoffs. To Mohsin — genuinely one of the great ones, a man who stayed bullish through eight different bear markets of his own creation. The ticker is retired. Position closed. We're all short without you.

arrivals.headline: The Replacements: Tom & Greg
arrivals.body: In exchange for Mohsin and Neil, the league welcomes Tom and Greg — and let's be honest about what happened here: this league lost color and gained a Pottery Barn catalog. Tom and Greg. TOM. AND. GREG. You cannot draft two whiter names. These are not fantasy managers, these are the guys who approve your mortgage. The seasoning cabinet just got swapped for a single jar of mayonnaise and the group chat's median hot-sauce tolerance dropped forty points overnight. The diversity report is in, and it's a blank page. Welcome, gentlemen — you have inherited a $1,000 FAAB budget, a full-savage roast column, and a Thanksgiving tradition that just got extremely complicated: Cowboys vs. Indians will be watched, reviewed, and litigated by this league on the fourth Thursday of November, and for the first time in franchise history, the Cowboys side has representation in the room. Draft accordingly.
